title: Executive, Outreach (Blood Donor Programme), 1-Year Part-Time Contract
description:
Job Type: Part-Time (12-month contract)

Working Hours: 8 hours per day

Work Schedule: 3-4 days per week

Work Days: Includes Saturday (fixed working day) and Sunday (as required)

Provide planning, development, and implementation of key activities and initiatives aimed at building up the national donor pool as well as maintaining and growing our pool of dedicated volunteers. Working in close partnership with key stakeholders from Blood Services Group (BSG) and Singapore Red Cross (SRC), she/he will recruit, mobilise and engage eligible volunteers to support relevant public education (outreach activities such as roadshows, learning journeys, blood donation talks etc.), donor engagement, tele-recruitment, and blood-donation-related activities. In addition, the incumbent will engage educational institutions, corporate, government, and community organisations to educate, recruit, retain, and recognise blood donors while supporting in organising community blood drives and group donations to build the national blood supply.

KEY RESPONSIBILITIES

● Collaborate with internal and external stakeholders to advocate on blood donation

● Undertake outreach and engagement activities towards expanding the donor pool (especially youths), including planning and organising roadshows, guided tours in the bloodbanks, blood donation talks etc

● Support in Conceptualising, planning and executing outreach activities to target audience (e.g members of public, students, staff) to raise awareness.

● Reach out to community partners (especially educational institutions) to arrange talks and learning journey to the bloodbanks.

● Handle the end-to-end programme management for all outreach activities and initiatives.

● Collaborate with partners and engage stakeholders for various initiatives.

● Work closely with the Head of Operations to develop and implement outreach strategies.

● Work closely with the operation team to engage internal and key stakeholders e.g educational institutions, corporate, government, and community organisations through outreach activities and initiatives to advocate on the National Blood Programme

● Work closely with the marketing team to develop collaterals, EDM, banners etc. for outreach activities and initiatives.

● Conduct relevant training to volunteers on blood donor recruitment to equip them with the relevant knowledge when volunteering for the outreach activities.

● Collaborate with internal and external stakeholders to promote blood donation and organise group donations at the bloodbanks.

● Undertake relevant administrative tasks, including but not limited to creating and maintaining volunteer and blood-drive records, updating SOPs and educational collateral etc.

● Assist in the planning for World Blood Donor Day 2026 event.

● Assist in the planning for National Blood Programme 80th Anniversary event.

● Prepare reports and provide prompt reporting to the management.

● Other duties as assigned.

JOB SPECIFICATION

Qualifications:

• Diploma in any discipline

Experience:

• Candidate(s) with a history of relevant voluntary/internship experience will have an added advantage Required experience, skills, and knowledge.

• Demonstrated interest in the non-profit/charity sector.

• Familiarity with the blood donation landscape and donor behaviour in Singapore.

• Experience in project or event management will be advantageous.

• Ability to prioritise work responsibilities/multitask, organise own work schedule.

• Think on the feet, make decisions and carry out responsibilities without the need for direct supervision.

• Communicate, negotiate, and engage professionally and confidently with people from all walks of life.

• Self-motivated, responsible, adopts a proactive approach to every aspect of work.

• Manage, grow, and utilise a team of volunteers from diverse backgrounds and with different interests/skillsets.

• Strong verbal and written communication skills, including the ability to tailor key messages and adopt different approaches for different audiences.

• Able to work from Tuesday to Saturday and occasionally on Sunday and some weekday evenings (when required).

• Able to deliver a high level of customer service skills and a keen eye for detail.

• Possesses Business-level proficiency in Microsoft Office.

title: Product Engineer
description:
About EDMI

EDMI is a global leader in smart metering and energy solutions. We are recognised internationally for our commitment to quality, reliability, compliance, and customer service. By combining advanced technology with strong engineering discipline and robust governance, EDMI delivers trusted solutions that support the future of energy worldwide.

About the Role
At EDMI, we develop and deliver innovative smart energy solutions worldwide. We are looking for a motivated Product Engineer to take ownership of assigned products from design to end-of-life. This role bridges R&D, manufacturing, and supply chain operations, ensuring smooth product introduction, continuous improvement, and lifecycle management.

You will play a key role in supporting NPI (New Product Introduction), prototype builds, managing production release, BOM/SAP processes, and coordinating with global teams to ensure product quality, cost efficiency, and on-time delivery.

Key Responsibilities

1. Product Lifecycle Ownership

  • Manage assigned products from design to end-of-life.
  • Prepare NPI schedules and ensure timely ramp-up to mass production.
  • Oversee product transfer from design to NPI and production across multiple sites.
  • Drive continuous improvement in cost, processes, and performance.

2.Production Release Governance

  • Drive cross-functional collaboration across R&D, Manufacturing, Quality, and Supply Chain teams.
  • Conduct production release reviews, ensuring documentation and approvals are complete.
  • Support manufacturing sites to achieve target yield during production release.

3.Prototype & Pilot Support

  • Coordinate cross-functional activities for prototype builds.
  • Collaborate with suppliers and purchasing teams for component readiness.
  • Collect DFM (Design for Manufacturability) and PFMEA data from pilot builds to feedback to design.
  • Ensure technical documentation is complete and up-to-date in databases.

4. Bill of Material (BOM), SAP & Engineering Change Notification (ECN) Management

  • Maintain SuperBOMs in SAP with EDMI-standard part numbers.
  • Work with Group Material Master team to ensure data accuracy.
  • Lead ECN meetings with stakeholders to manage product changes according to procedure.

5. Test Development Support

  • Partner with Test Development team to support product verification and qualification activities.
  • Identify and implement process improvements to optimise product cost and efficiency.
  • Analyse test data to identify improvement opportunities to enhance test efficiency and product quality.
  • Implement initiatives to optimise test performance and improve production yield through corrective and preventive actions.

What We’re Looking For

  • Bachelor’s degree in Electrical or Electronics Engineering (Diploma holders with relevant experience welcome).
  • 3–5 years of experience in product engineering or NPI preferred (fresh graduates considered).
  • Experience in technical design and product transfer within the Electronics industry is a strong plus.
  • Strong multitasking, analytical, and computer skills.
  • Willingness to travel frequently between Singapore and Malaysia.
  • Strong interpersonal and stakeholder management skills.

description:
This is a Merit-Only campaign and we are not looking to appoint anyone until a position becomes available at a future date. We intend to place all candidates who reach the benchmark on a Merit List.

Working Arrangements & Further Information

The MoJ offers Hybrid Working arrangements where business need allows. This is an informal, non-contractual form of flexible working that blends working from your base location, different MoJ sites and / or from home (please be aware that this role can only be worked in the UK and not overseas). Some roles will not be suitable for Hybrid Working. Similarly, Hybrid Working will not suit everyone’s circumstances. Arrangements will be discussed and agreed with the successful candidate(s) and subject to regular review.

For nationally advertised roles, the successful candidate(s) will be appointed to a MoJ office location, which may include their nearest Justice Collaboration Centre or Justice Satellite Office. This will be discussed and agreed on the completion of pre-employment checks.

Some of MoJ’s terms and conditions of service are changing as part of Civil Service reform. The changes will apply to staff joining MoJ who are new to the Civil Service. Staff joining MoJ from other civil service employers will transfer onto the new MoJ terms if they are already on 'modernised' terms in their current post or onto 'unmodernised' MoJ terms if they are on 'unmodernised' terms at their current post. Details will be available if an offer is made.

Standard full time working hours are 37 hours per week excluding breaks which are unpaid. HMPPS welcomes part-time, flexible and job-sharing working patterns, where they meet the demands of the role and business needs. All applications for part-time, flexible and job-sharing working patterns will be considered in accordance with the HMPPS’ Flexible Working policy.

If you are a current NPS employee, this vacancy may be available on a Loan basis for up to 2 years. Applications are invited from suitable qualified staff.

The Loan/Secondment is subject to the approval of the selected candidate's Business Unit, which should be obtained before confirmation of appointment.

Benefits

Annual Leave

-The holiday year runs from 1 March. If you work a non standard work pattern your leave entitlement may be expressed in either hours or days as appropriate. Leave entitlement is calculated on a pro-rata basis and you will be advised of your actual entitlement on appointment. If you were appointed internally and your leave was previously calculated in days, this will continue to be the case.

Bank, Public and Privilege Holidays

-You are entitled to 9 days (66 hours 36 minutes) in recognition of bank, public and privilege holidays. These hours are added to your annual leave allowance. There is a requirement to work some public and bank holidays subject to your shift pattern and the operational needs of the establishment

Pension

-The Civil Service offers a choice of two pension schemes, giving you the flexibility to choose the pension that suits you best.

Work Life Balance

HM Prison & Probation Service (HMPPS) is keen to encourage alternative working arrangements. Work life balance provides greater opportunities for staff to work more flexibly wherever managers and establishments can accommodate requests to do so. HMPPS offers flexible working subject to completion of a satisfactory probationary period and NVQ

Season Ticket Advance

-After two months’ service, you’ll be eligible to apply for a season ticket advance to purchase a quarterly or longer-period season ticket for travel between home and your place of work

Childcare Vouchers

For any moves across the Civil Service may have implications on your ability to carry on claiming childcare vouchers

Training

HMPPS is committed to staff development and offers a range of training and development opportunities, including areas such as Equality and Diversity, Dealing with Challenging Behaviour, Suicide Prevention and Anti Bullying Programmes

-There are opportunities to access promotion programmes and HMPPS provides a variety of training appropriate to individual posts

-All staff receive security and diversity training and an individual induction programme into their new roles

Eligibility

-All candidates are subject to security and identity checks prior to taking up post

-All external candidates are subject to 6 months probation. Internal candidates are subject to probation if they have not already served a probationary period within HMPPS

-All staff are required to declare whether they are a member of a group or organisation which the HMPPS considers to be racist

Working for the Civil Service

The Civil Service Code sets out the standards of behaviour expected of civil servants.

We recruit by merit on the basis of fair and open competition, as outlined in the Civil Service Commission's recruitment principles. Should you feel that the recruitment process has breached the recruitment principles you are able to raise a formal complaint in the following order

  • To Transformative Business Services (0345 241 5358 (Monday to Friday 8am - 6pm) or e mail moj-recruitment-vetting-enquiries@resourcing.soprasteria.co.uk);
  • To Ministry of Justice Resourcing team (resourcing-management-office@justice.gov.uk);
  • To the Civil Service Commission (details available here)

As a Disability Confident employer, MoJ are committed to providing everyone with the opportunity to demonstrate their skills, talent and abilities, by making adjustments throughout all elements of the recruitment process and in the workplace. MoJ are able to offer an interview to disabled candidates who meet the minimum selection criteria, except in a limited number of campaigns.

You will be able to request reasonable adjustments to the recruitment process within the application form. If you need additional help completing the application form, please contact the TBS Recruitment Enquiries Team.

For more information on applying for a role as a candidate with a disability or long-term condition, please watch our animated videos.

Diversity & Inclusion

The Civil Service is committed to attract, retain and invest in talent wherever it is found. To learn more please see the Civil Service People Plan and the Civil Service Diversity and Inclusion Strategy.

A Great Place to Work for Veterans

The "Making the Civil Service a Great Place to work for veterans" initiative includes a guaranteed interview scheme to those who meet the minimum criteria to provide eligible former members of the Armed Forces with opportunities to secure rewarding jobs. Allowing veterans to continue to serve their country, and to bring highly skilled individuals with a broad range of experience into the Civil Service in an environment, which recognises and values your previous service in the Armed Forces.
For further details about the initiative and eligibility requirements visit:

Redeployment Interview Scheme

Civil Service departments are expected to explore redeployment opportunities before making an individual redundant. The MoJ is committed, as part of the Redeployment Interview Scheme, to providing opportunities to those who are 'at risk of redundancy'.

MoJ is able to offer an interview to eligible candidates who meet the minimum selection criteria, except in a limited number of campaigns. Candidates will not be eligible for the Redeployment Interview Scheme if they are applying on promotion.

Civil Service Nationality Rules

This job is broadly open to the following groups:

  • UK nationals
  • nationals of the Republic of Ireland
  • nationals of Commonwealth countries who have the right to work in the UK
  • nationals of the EU, Switzerland, Norway, Iceland or Liechtenstein and family members of those nationalities with settled or pre-settled status under the European Union Settlement Scheme (EUSS) (opens in a new window) https://www.gov.uk/settled-status-eu-citizens-families

  • Turkish nationals, and certain family members of Turkish nationals, who have accrued the right to work in the Civil Service

Further information on nationality requirements (opens in a new window) https://www.gov.uk/government/publications/nationality-rules

Reserve list

A reserve list may be held for up to 12 months from which further appointments may be made for the same or similar roles.

PAY AWARD PENDING AT 3.3% salary will increase to £49,817 - £53,051 per annum/pro rata for part time


Are you passionate about supporting people to achieve the best possible outcomes and live independently for as long as possible?

Are you excited by the opportunity to be part of a brand-new service and help shape the way it develops?

If so, we would love to hear from you.

About the Role

We have a full-time Social Work Lead position available within our new Community Reablement Service.

This is an exciting opportunity to join an innovative countywide service at the beginning of its journey and play a key role in shaping how the service develops and delivers positive outcomes for the people of Gloucestershire.

As a Social Work Lead, you will provide professional leadership, supervision and support to Social Workers, Social Care Practitioners, and Reablement Co-ordinators across the service. You will promote excellent practice, supporting staff to deliver strengths-based, person-centred interventions that maximise independence and wellbeing.

Working as part of an integrated multidisciplinary team, you will play a key role in supporting adults at a critical stage in their journey. You will help ensure people experience a seamless transition from reablement into longer-term support where required.

You will be expected to promote a culture of professional curiosity, reflective practice and continuous improvement, encouraging accountability while role modelling best practice in your own work.

A key aspect of the role will be supporting practitioners to manage complex situations involving risk, safeguarding, mental capacity and decision-making. You will coordinate and oversee safeguarding enquiries in line with the Care Act 2014, provide professional advice and guidance, and support practitioners to deliver high-quality outcomes for adults with care and support needs.

This role offers a unique opportunity to influence the development of a brand-new service, helping to shape processes, embed best practice and support the growth of a highly skilled workforce.

A key focus of this role will be supporting the service's Front Door Hub. The Front Door Hub acts as the central point for referrals into the Community Reablement Service and receives referrals from a wide range of stakeholders, including health professionals, Adult Social Care teams, community services and partner organisations. Working alongside colleagues within the Front Door Hub, you will coordinate and oversee incoming referrals, gathering and analysing information to determine the most appropriate pathway and response for each individual. This will involve identifying whether a person is suitable for reablement support, allocating work across the service, and ensuring timely decision-making.

About the Service

Our Community Reablement Service has been designed to help people regain confidence, skills and independence following a change in circumstances.

The service brings together professionals from a range of disciplines, working as one team to support people to achieve what matters most to them. Our focus is on enabling people to do as much as possible for themselves, building on strengths, promoting resilience and connecting people with their communities.

As a Social Work Lead, you will play a key role in embedding strengths-based practice across the service, supporting practitioners to deliver high-quality Care Act assessments, support planning, safeguarding interventions and person-centred decision-making.

You will also contribute to service development, helping to establish and refine new ways of working that support excellent practice and deliver outstanding outcomes.

About You

To join us, you must:

  • Hold a recognised Social Work qualification and be registered with Social Work England.

  • Have successfully completed your ASYE and have significant post-qualifying experience within Adult Social Care.

  • Have experience of supervising, mentoring or supporting the professional development of Social Workers and other practitioners.

  • Have excellent knowledge of the Care Act 2014, Mental Capacity Act 2005, Human Rights legislation and Adult Safeguarding responsibilities.

  • Have experience of supporting or leading complex safeguarding enquiries and risk management processes.

  • Demonstrate strong analytical skills and professional judgement when working with complex situations and competing risks.

  • Be committed to strengths-based, person-centred practice and supporting people to maximise their independence.

  • Have excellent communication and relationship-building skills, with the ability to influence, coach and support others.

  • Be able to prioritise effectively and work confidently within a fast-paced and evolving environment.

  • Be enthusiastic about service development and helping shape an innovative new model of support.

Our values are at the heart of everything we do and how we treat each other. They provide essential guiding principles about the way that we work and set the tone for our culture, and identify what we, as an organisation, care about. See more about our Values on our website.

If you hold the same behaviours and approach, then we want to hear from you! In exchange, we will provide you with full training and support to help you succeed in your role.

Why Join Us?

As part of our new Community Reablement Service, you will:

  • Help shape and influence the development of a new countywide service.

  • Provide professional leadership and support to a skilled multidisciplinary workforce.

  • Champion strengths-based social work practice, safeguarding and professional development.

  • Support the development of innovative approaches that improve outcomes and maximise independence.

  • Work within a supportive and collaborative environment that values creativity, learning and continuous improvement.

  • Make a meaningful difference to the lives of adults across Gloucestershire every day.

Gloucestershire County Council provides the following rewards package in return for your hard work:

  • Option to purchase up to 10 days of additional leave per year (pro rata for part time employees)

title: Assistant Director (Field Governance)
description:
[What the role is]

The Assistant Director (Field Governance) leads the Field Governance Office (FGO) within the GCD Office, serving as the subject matter specialist across one or more functional domains — Finance, Procurement, Revenue, Grants Management, or Charity Governance. You will translate headquarters policies into practical guidance for constituency offices, strengthen compliance standards across Grassroots Organisation (GRO) operations, and partner with the Grassroots Services Division to build governance capability at the ground level.

[What you will be working on]

  • Governance Advisory and Compliance — Lead the FGO in providing oversight, guidance, and advisory support to Constituency Office (CO) staff and GROs on financial, procurement, and governance matters to ensure compliance with applicable rules, regulations, and standard operating procedures.
  • Financial Management and Reporting — Oversee the financial controls and accounts of GROs, ensuring accuracy, timeliness, and compliance with reporting requirements; identify process weaknesses and drive improvements through data analytics and digital solutions.
  • Procurement and Revenue Oversight — Oversee procurement and revenue-earning activities across the GRC to ensure value for money, regulatory compliance, and sound governance; surface control weaknesses through data analytics and contribute to the continuous improvement of procurement practices.
  • Charity Governance and Grants Management — Oversee charity governance, fundraising, and grants management activities to ensure compliance with regulatory requirements; review key submissions and disbursement processes; and work with the Grassroots Services Division to strengthen related policies and practices.
  • Audit and Risk Management — Coordinate audit activities, oversee the management of audit findings, and ensure CO staff are prepared and equipped to meet audit requirements; conduct regular checks to promote a culture of compliance and sound risk management.
  • Training and Capability Development — Build governance capability across CO staff and Grassroots Leaders (GRLs) through training workshops, advisory support, and knowledge-sharing initiatives, in collaboration with NACLI and the Grassroots Services Division.
  • Subject Matter Specialisation — Develop and maintain deep expertise in one core functional area — Finance Operations, Procurement, Charity and Grants, or Revenue Management — to serve as the designated subject matter specialist within the CDD, providing specialised guidance to fellow FGO leads and contributing to policy development within the area of specialisation.

[What we are looking for]

· Experience: At least five years of working experience in a management role, with a track record of overseeing governance, financial management, procurement, or audit functions

· Skills (Must-have): Sound knowledge of financial governance, procurement regulations, and grants management; strong analytical skills with the ability to identify control weaknesses and drive improvements; ability to translate policy requirements into clear, practical operational guidance; meticulous with strong attention to detail; and effective interpersonal and stakeholder engagement skills

· Skills (Good to have): Familiarity with digital tools such as RPA or data analytics platforms; experience in field operations or community development environment; and prior exposure to charity governance or GRO financial management

title: Research Associate  (Molecular Ecology/Bioinformatics)
description:
Overview

This post will primarily support the work of the NERC Environmental Omics Facility (NEOF), based in the Genomics Laboratory of the Ecology and Evolutionary Biology cluster in the School of Biosciences, but also a number of research projects based in the Laboratory. The Genomics Laboratory is led by Professor Terry Burke and the NEOF Visitor Facility is led by Professor Jon Slate.

NEOF in Sheffield supports environmental omics research across the UK, with responsibility for supporting the laboratory work of users who access the NEOF Visitor Facility. Visiting researchers receive training while undertaking their own analyses. NEOF supports a range of molecular techniques to tackle research questions in environmental, ecological and evolutionary biology, but has expertise in genome sequencing, marker analysis, population genomics, evolutionary genetics, pedigree analysis, metabarcoding and the detection and interpretation of environmental DNA and RNA. It has outstanding facilities and equipment to support this work, including access to a full range of sequencing, genotyping and DNA preparation technologies, robotics, clean rooms and high-performance computing.

The appointee will deliver existing on-line and in-person regular training courses in a range of bioinformatics, develop new training modules, assist NEOF users with the analysis of their datasets, and contribute to research projects including, for example, the detection of rare or endangered species in environmental samples, using low-coverage genome sequencing methods in studies of avian life history, assembling de-novo genomes, and investigating the role of inversions in natural populations of non-model species.

Applicants should have a PhD (or be close to completion / have equivalent postdoctoral level work experience) in molecular ecology or evolutionary genetics, including genetic analyses (for example, diet analysis, studies of biodiversity, eDNA, population structure, mating systems, linkage mapping, genome assembly, comparative genomics or phylogenetics) and possess excellent analytical skills. Programming skills (e.g., Linux, R, PYTHON or PERL) and experience of high-performance computing clusters are also essential.

Main duties and responsibilities

  • Liaise with the Director of the NEOF Visitor Facility in Sheffield and Facility staff in Sheffield and Liverpool over work schedules and progress

  • Support NEOF staff and users with data analysis and bioinformatics

  • Deliver and develop training in the analysis of genomic data

  • Provide feedback on enquiries and applications to use the Facility, including cost estimates

  • Provide feedback on Facility-supported work and manuscripts

  • Produce optimised easy-to-follow protocols and pipelines or computer scripts to enable staff and users with appropriate statistical and molecular population genetic tools

  • Establish and maintain appropriate databases for managing and curating NEOF and Genomics Facility data, samples, and projects

  • Ensure that the tools used by the Facility remain at the cutting edge and keep up to date with latest techniques and analyses

  • Conduct agreed research and development activities that lead to published outputs

  • Continuously monitor and check progress of Facility projects; the unpredictability of research means that daily planning needs to accommodate new developments

  • Assist with the administration of NEOF and lab activities in the University’s High-Performance Computing facility

  • Represent NEOF at occasional external activities such as workshops and conferences

  • Other tasks to ensure the efficient functioning, success, and development of the NEOF Visitor Facility and the host laboratory, as required

  • As a member of staff you will be encouraged to make ethical decisions in your role, embedding the University sustainability strategy into your working activities wherever possible.

  • Carry out other duties, commensurate with the grade and remit of the post

As a Postdoctoral Research Associate, you will be working on an exciting project that assesses the feasibility of producing protein emulsifiers for use in the food industry.

There is an urgent need from food manufacturers and consumers for clean-label naturally derived emulsifier alternatives to synthetic or unsustainable natural sources. The global market

product ranges away from synthetic additives. The project will involve engagement with industry and address research under the Engineering for Health theme of the School carried out at the University.

  • Collaborate across geographically distributed teams in Hungary, the United States, and other global locations.

  • Contribute to engineering best practices around scalability, reliability, security, observability, performance, and automated testing.

  • Represent Cloudera in relevant open source communities, contributing upstream where appropriate.

  • BS/MS in Computer Science or a related field, and/or 8+ years of relevant software engineering experience.

  • Strong understanding of software architecture, distributed systems, design patterns, and engineering best practices.

  • Strong Java skills and extensive experience across the Java ecosystem.

  • Experience with Kubernetes and Docker and modern cloud-native architectures.

description:

Perform high-speed simulation and signal integrity analysis for AI server platforms, collaborating with cross-functional teams to optimize high-speed interfaces and support testing through to mass production.

  • Utilize simulation tools such as Ansys HFSS/SIwave, Cadence Sigrity, Keysight ADS, or equivalents for signal integrity analysis.
  • Interpret S-parameters, insertion/return loss, crosstalk, jitter, eye diagrams, and channel modeling to diagnose and improve signal paths.
  • Perform high-speed PCB simulation and lab validation to confirm design integrity.

Preferred competencies and qualifications

  • Experience with high-density GPU server platforms, such as enterprise HGX or accelerator architectures, to support advanced computing environments.

When joining Sizewell C, you may wonder why you are contacted by colleagues with an EDF email or see the EDF logo on portals that you access and/or documentation you receive; this is because we have partnered with EDF for the provision of a number of support services whilst we complete a successful transition out of the EDF group.

This role is ideal for a local candidate looking to develop their career in data and digital analytics while contributing to one of the UK's most significant infrastructure and clean energy projects.

Sizewell C is looking for a Health, Safety, Wellbeing Data & Digital Analyst to help transform how HSW data is managed, analysed and reported across a nationally significant infrastructure project.Working closely with the Health & Safety Systems and Visualisation Manager, you'll use Power BI, Excel, Power Automate and Power Apps to turn data into meaningful insights that support safer working, better decision-making and continuous improvement.

  • Develop dashboards, reports and performance metrics using Power BI.

  • Experience working with data, reporting, business intelligence or digital systems.

  • Excellent communication and organisational skills.

Desirable

  • Excel and Power BI skills.
  • Experience with Power Automate and Power Apps.
  • Experience within construction, infrastructure, energy, utilities or health & safety
    environments.
  • Data analytics, Power BI or Microsoft certifications.

Why Join Sizewell C?

  • Be part of one of the UK's most ambitious clean energy projects.
  • Work on innovative digital solutions that influence project performance.
  • Excellent salary, bonus and pension package.
  • Career development opportunities.

Ready to Make an Impact?

If you're passionate about data, digital innovation, health, safety and wellbeing, we'd love to hear from you.

Apply now and help shape the future of UK energy through data, insight and innovation.

Sizewell C’s business is to design, finance, construct, commission, operate, maintain, and eventually decommission the nuclear power plant and related infrastructure at Sizewell C in Suffolk. Overall, whilst the Company is in the construction phase, the Boards’ principal focus is on the development and construction of Sizewell C on time, on budget and to the highest quality and safety standards. The Company is maturing to meet all these requirements.

Sizewell C is economically regulated by OFGEM under the RAB model similar to other UK electricity distribution networks and Thames Tideway.

Sizewell C construction strategy is to replicate the design of Hinkley Point C, using the majority of the same supply chain, but innovating in the way it is delivered to achieve savings in time and cost of around 20%. The CCO will need to be guided by and incorporate lessons learned from the Hinkley Point C commercial delivery to achieve Sizewell C’s ambition.

Following Financial Completion and Revenue Commencement, Sizewell C is fully funded and is owned by; The Secretary of State for Energy Security and Net Zero representing HM Government, La Caisse, Centrica, EDF and Amber Infrastructure.

title: DAC Centre Supervisor
description:
Role Summary

The DAC Centre Supervisor is responsible for overseeing the daily operations and service delivery of the Multiple Disability Day Activity Centre (DAC), ensuring clients receive safe, person-centred and meaningful care and activity support. The role combines operational leadership with Occupational Therapy principles to promote clients’ functional abilities, independence, participation and quality of life. The Supervisor works closely with care staff, caregivers, Allied Health Professionals and other stakeholders to develop and implement programmes that meet individual needs and goals and reports monthly to the Head of Therapy on operational and programme matters.


Key Responsibilities

• Supervise daily DAC operations and services ensuring safe, effective and efficient service delivery and appropriate care for clients with multiple and complex disabilities.

• Apply Occupational Therapy principles to develop and create programs and activities to support functional abilities, activities of daily living, independence, sensory needs, mobility, positioning, adaptive equipment and community participation.

• Perform & complete all relevant documentation of annual functional assessments and contribute to engage all clients in their daily individualised activity, sensory, functional, social and community participation programmes.

• Collaborate with Occupational Therapists, Physiotherapists, Speech and Language Therapists, psychologists, nurses, social workers, training officers and other professionals to provide holistic, person-centred support, care and services.

• Supervise, coach and guide care staff (care-coordinator, care associate and therapy aides) in safe transfers, positioning, mobility, daily activities, sensory and behavioural support, and appropriate use of adaptive equipment.

• Monitor client participation, progress and responses; ensure appropriate documentation, follow-up and communication with clients, caregivers and families by working collaboratively with social workers.

• Promote positive behavioural support and ensure safeguarding, risk management and incident-reporting requirements are followed.

• Participate and provide inputs for monthly MDT meetings.

• Maintain accurate client records, attendance, care plans, assessments, programme documentation and administrative records.

• Ensure SOPs and workflows are reviewed and updated, with approval from the Head of Therapy/CEO where required.

• Oversee operational resources, budget, inventory, procurement, equipment maintenance and asset management with approval from the Head of Therapy/CEO.

• Coordinate safe and appropriate transport arrangements for clients and monitor the suitability of therapy, mobility, sensory and activity equipment.

• Support staff orientation, training, competency development and performance supervision.

• Assist with audits, regulatory requirements, quality improvement and service development initiatives.

• Promote a culture of dignity, inclusion, respect, empowerment and meaningful participation.

• Passionate to adopt and apply holistic care philosophy and person centric practice at work for DAC residents, with alignment of service needs at organisational level.


Skills & Qualifications

• Bachelor’s degree in occupational therapy with AHPC Full registration.

• 3–5 years and above of relevant experience in disability services, rehabilitation, community care, special needs or healthcare, preferably with supervisory or service coordination experience.

• Experience supporting individuals with intellectual, physical, multiple or complex disabilities in Day Activity Centre, Adult Disability Home, Nursing Home and Residential Home will be an additional advantage.

• Strong understanding of person-centred care, safeguarding, risk management, positive behavioural support and multidisciplinary practice.

• Strong communication, leadership, organisational, problem-solving, documentation, budgeting and programme-planning skills.

• Ability to coach and develop care staff and coordinate effectively across professional disciplines.

• Commitment to promoting client dignity, independence, inclusion, participation and quality of life.

title: LCL Operations Agent SAI
description:
About Maersk

At Maersk, we have embarked on a transformation journey to become the global integrator of container logistics, connecting and simplifying our customers’ supply chains from end to end.

With a presence across the globe, our people are at the heart of our business. We are committed to creating an inclusive and collaborative environment where talented individuals can grow, make an impact, and build a career in global logistics.

If you are passionate about freight forwarding, enjoy solving operational challenges, and thrive in a fast-paced customer-focused environment, this could be the opportunity for you.

About the Role

We are looking for an LCL Operations Agent to join our team in Durban.

In this role, you will be responsible for managing the end-to-end operational lifecycle of LCL import and export shipments, from booking through to final delivery and invoicing.

You will work closely with customers, shipping lines, transport providers, warehouses, customs brokers, co-loaders, overseas offices, and internal teams to ensure shipments move efficiently, accurately, and in line with customer expectations.

This is an operationally focused role where attention to detail, ownership, proactive communication, and strong freight-forwarding knowledge are essential to success.

Key Responsibilities

Shipment Coordination & Execution

  • Manage LCL import and export shipments from booking through final delivery.

  • Coordinate cargo collection, warehouse handling, consolidation, deconsolidation, customs release, and final distribution.

  • Arrange bookings with shipping lines, co-loaders, transport providers, depots, and warehouses.

  • Monitor shipment milestones and proactively track cargo movement.

  • Identify potential delays or disruptions and take corrective action.

  • Maintain accurate shipment updates in operational systems.

  • Ensure shipments are executed in accordance with customer requirements and company standards.

Documentation & Compliance

  • Prepare, review, and process operational and shipping documentation accurately and within required timelines.

  • Manage documentation including Bills of Lading, Cargo Manifests, Shipping Instructions, Delivery Orders, Arrival Notices, and customs/regulatory documentation.

  • Ensure compliance with local and international trade requirements.

  • Maintain accurate shipment records and filing systems.

  • Work with customs brokers and relevant authorities to facilitate smooth cargo clearance.

  • Verify documentation to minimize delays, penalties, and service disruptions.

Customer Service & Stakeholder Management

  • Act as a key operational contact throughout the shipment lifecycle.

  • Provide proactive updates on shipment status, transit progress, delays, and delivery schedules.

  • Respond to customer queries professionally and in a timely manner.

  • Manage escalations and resolve operational issues effectively.

  • Build strong relationships with customers and internal and external stakeholders.

  • Collaborate with Customer Service, Sales, Finance, Compliance, and Customs teams.

Financial & Administrative Activities

  • Verify supplier invoices and operational costs against agreed rates.

  • Support accurate customer billing and revenue recognition.

  • Ensure accurate shipment costing within operational systems.

  • Maintain operational records and reports.

  • Support KPI monitoring, performance analysis, and cost-control initiatives.

Continuous Improvement

  • Identify opportunities to improve operational efficiency, productivity, and service quality.

  • Participate in operational reviews and improvement projects.

  • Contribute to best practices within LCL operations.

  • Promote a culture of accountability, operational excellence, and customer-centric service.

What We’re Looking For

The ideal candidate will bring:

  • Strong knowledge of freight forwarding and LCL operations.

  • Practical experience handling import and export shipments.

  • Good understanding of shipping documentation, customs processes, and Incoterms.

  • Experience with forwarding operations, shipment invoicing, and operational costing.

  • Strong organizational and planning skills.

  • Excellent attention to detail and accuracy.

  • Strong communication and stakeholder-management skills.

  • A proactive, customer-focused approach.

  • Strong analytical and problem-solving abilities.

  • Ability to manage multiple priorities and work effectively under pressure.

  • Good computer literacy and experience using freight-forwarding systems.

  • Qualifications & Experience

    Essential:

  • Matric / Grade 12.

  • Diploma or Degree in Logistics, Supply Chain Management, International Trade, or a related field is advantageous.

  • Minimum 2 years of relevant employment experience in freight forwarding, logistics, and/or LCL operations.

  • Proven experience coordinating import and export shipments.

  • Working knowledge of shipping lines, transport providers, customs processes, and freight-forwarding operations.

  • Strong understanding of international shipping documentation.

  • Ocean freight and LCL experience are essential.

​

Advantageous:

  • Experience in both LCL and FCL operations.

  • Cross-border experience.

  • Experience within a multinational freight-forwarding environment.

  • Knowledge of international trade regulations and customs compliance.

  • Experience using CargoWise.

What Success Looks Like

Your success in this role will be measured through:

  • On-time shipment processing and delivery.

  • Customer satisfaction and service quality.

  • Documentation accuracy and compliance.

  • Achievement of shipment milestones.

  • Billing and costing accuracy.

  • Operational productivity and efficiency.

  • Effective resolution of shipment exceptions and escalations.

  • Compliance with company and regulatory requirements.

Why Join Maersk?

At Maersk, you will become part of a global organization where you can work with colleagues and customers across different markets and cultures.

We offer an environment where collaboration, accountability, continuous learning, and innovation are encouraged. You will have the opportunity to develop your logistics expertise while contributing to the smooth movement of cargo and the success of our customers’ supply chains.

· Conduct or support both intertidal and marine field surveys.

Education and Experience

Knowledge andSkills

title: Research Associate: Neuroscience (2 Posts)
description:
Overview

Why are brains the way they are? Do neural circuits function in an “optimal” way, and if so, in what sense are they optimal? How does the brain encode sensory information and form associative memories? Andrew Lin’s lab at the University of Sheffield is seeking up to two Research Associates to study these questions in the fruit fly Drosophila.

We study memory using a range of methods, such as in vivo two-photon calcium imaging, electrophysiology, fly genetics, behavioural experiments, computational modelling and building custom equipment. You will design, develop and perform experiments and data analysis (tailoring the project to your own interests and expertise), write papers, and present your work at conferences and seminars.

We seek self-motivated, innovative and creative candidates with a PhD (or be close to completion / have equivalent postdoctoral level experience) in a relevant field, expertise in at least some of the above techniques, excellent communication skills, and an ability to work independently and in a team. We encourage applications from diverse academic backgrounds, such as biology, neuroscience, experimental psychology, computer science, physics and engineering.



Main duties and responsibilities

  • Record neural activity in Drosophila using imaging and/or electrophysiology.

  • Design and carry out protocols to induce neuronal plasticity via learning and/or homeostatic plasticity.

  • Carry out behavioural experiments to measure learning and relate neural activity to behaviour.

  • Design and carry out Drosophila crossing schemes to create desired transgenic flies.

  • Analyse and record data using established methods and/or design new custom methods for data analysis.

  • Set up and maintain lab equipment.

  • Prepare papers for journals/presentations either in-hours or at national/international conferences or seminars to disseminate research findings.

  • Write supporting documents to contribute to and support the work of the Research Group, e.g., manuscripts for publication and grant applications.

  • Plan for specific aspects of the research programme.

  • If given a particular hypothesis to examine, plan for own contribution up to 3 months ahead, incorporating issues such as the availability of resources, deadlines, project milestones and overall research aims. Design individual experiments weekly.

  • Co-ordinate and liaise with other members of the research group over work progress.

  • Supervise research team/activities if required.

  • Continuously monitor and check results. The unpredictability of research means that daily planning needs to accommodate new developments.

  • Read academic papers, journals and textbooks and attend conferences to keep abreast of developments.

  • Contribute to the supervision of PhD students and other team members within the group.

  • Carry out administrative roles as required, e.g., ordering reagents.

title: QC Technician
description:
The QC Technician supports the local QC function by carrying out sample preparation, physical and appearance checks, sieve checks, powder mixing / dissolution checks, result follow-up, external laboratory coordination and general laboratory operations.

The role helps ensure that raw materials (RM) and finished goods (FG) are checked, tested and followed up in a timely, accurate and food-safety-compliant manner so that RM / FG release can be completed without unnecessary delay.

Responsibilities:
Sample management and testing support

  • Receive, label, prepare and organise RM / FG samples for QC checks and external laboratory testing.
  • Support sample registration, sample tracking and testing priority follow-up.
  • Prepare samples for physical checks, sieve checks, powder mixing / dissolution checks, solubility / appearance checks and investigation comparisons.
  • Send raw material and finished goods samples to external laboratories for testing where required.
  • Follow up with external laboratories on pending results and testing status.
  • Perform and document internal physical and appearance checks on RM / FG samples, including colour, appearance, lumps, black particles, sieve condition, solubility and other visible abnormalities.
  • Carry out sieve checks, powder mixing / dissolution checks and visual inspections to identify potential issues such as lumps, black particles, unusual colour / appearance, floating particles, residue, settling or other visible abnormalities.
  • Record observations clearly in the QC checklist / tracker, including photos or comparison samples where required, so that abnormal findings can be reviewed and traced properly.
  • Escalate any abnormal finding, borderline observation, inconsistent result, missing information or urgent release concern promptly to the QC Manager / QC Executive before any release decision is made.

COA and result follow-up support

  • Assist in checking and compiling test results for RM / FG release.
  • Support COA preparation and result entry under the guidance of the QC Manager / QC Executive.
  • Ensure QC records, sample records and result follow-up trackers are updated accurately.
  • Highlight urgent release priorities and testing delays that may affect production or customer commitments.

Food safety, FSSC 22000 and compliance

  • Perform QC tasks in accordance with company SOPs, FSSC 22000 food safety management system requirements, GMP, hygiene and contamination prevention practices.
  • Apply basic food safety awareness when handling samples, laboratory materials, equipment and documents.
  • Report sample abnormalities, potential contamination concerns, hygiene issues, equipment issues or unsafe conditions promptly.
  • Maintain accurate and traceable records to support audit readiness and safe product release.
  • Support audit preparation and follow-up actions where QC involvement is required.

Laboratory operations

  • Maintain good laboratory housekeeping, cleanliness and sample organisation.
  • Support routine checks of QC equipment and laboratory condition.
  • Coordinate or support equipment calibration follow-up where required.
  • Manage basic lab consumables and highlight replenishment needs.
  • Support proper storage and disposal of laboratory chemicals, samples and waste in accordance with safety requirements.
  • Assist during investigations, retesting, sample comparison and complaint-related checks.

About You:

  • NITEC, Higher NITEC or Diploma in Chemistry, Food Science, Biotechnology, Pharmaceutical Science or a related scientific discipline.

  • Minimum 1 to 3 years of relevant experience in QC, laboratory, food manufacturing, food ingredients, pharmaceutical, nutraceutical or related environment.

  • Fresh candidates with relevant scientific education, good attitude and willingness to learn may be considered.

  • Basic knowledge or awareness of food safety, GMP, hygiene, HACCP or FSSC 22000 requirements is preferred.

  • Basic understanding of sample handling, physical checks, laboratory documentation and COA support is preferred.

  • Experience in food ingredient or premix manufacturing environment is an advantage.

  • Able to follow SOPs and maintain accurate records.

  • Good attention to detail and careful working habits.

  • Able to communicate in English and coordinate with internal teams.

  • Basic Microsoft Office skills, especially Excel and Outlook.

  • Willing to perform hands-on laboratory and sample handling work.

  • Candidates must be eligible to work in Singapore; this role does not provide sponsorship.
